description:
Site 3 of fz-nml.9. prim.rs:2238 boxes the PID extern result and fz_send unboxes it at once: send(self(), :ping) 0/1000/1000; with the pid hoisted 0/1/1. This is the box fz-sc8.167 once listed.

Scope redirected by the user 2026-11-17 (relayed by JSON, verbatim: "yes, redirect it. pids like atoms."): a pid ref word packs the pid in its payload bits, as an atom ref packs its id. Boxing a pid is a pack and never allocates; load_opaque_word(PID) reads the payload; no ScalarBox ever holds a pid. REF (make_ref, a 64-bit counter) is out of scope and stays boxed.

Files: runtime any_value.rs, heap/imp.rs, ref_io.rs, gc, deep_copy.rs, term*.rs, ir_runtime.rs; compiler native_codegen (prim, receive, fn_ctx, repr), jobs/native.rs, ir_interp value + extern_call, telemetry/value.rs, runtime_type_predicate.rs, dispatch_matrix/pattern.rs; docs; fixture 01705.

Acceptance: send(self(), :ping) allocates no pid box on any path (interp, JIT, AOT agree); pins lowered where they fall; nothing rises.

Earlier scope (withdrawn): native self() feeds fz_send a raw pid word via CodegenValue::Known. Census and probes: fz-nml.9 description (JSON session, develop 4a05ae2be; per 1000 steps interp/run/build).
title: A pid is packed into its ref word, as an atom is
